questions.stem: An element has the electronic configuration 2,8,7. What is its position in the periodic table and what type of ion will it most likely form?

options.text: Period 3, Group 7; it will form a 1- ion
Period 7, Group 3; it will form a 3+ ion
Period 3, Group 7; it will form a 7+ ion
Period 2, Group 8; it will form no ions

questions.explanation: The element has 3 electron shells (Period 3) and 7 outer electrons (Group 7). This is chlorine. Group 7 elements gain 1 electron to achieve a full outer shell, forming 1- ions (e.g., Cl⁻). They do not lose all 7 outer electrons as this would require far too much energy.

questions.stem: Element X has 12 electrons. A student writes its electronic configuration as 2,10. What is wrong, and what is the correct configuration?

options.text: Nothing is wrong; 2,10 is correct
The second shell can only hold 8 electrons, so it should be 2,8,2
The first shell can hold 8 electrons, so it should be 8,4
Each shell holds 2 electrons, so it should be 2,2,2,2,2,2

questions.explanation: The first electron shell holds a maximum of 2 electrons, the second holds a maximum of 8. The student tried to put 10 in the second shell, exceeding its capacity. The correct configuration for element 12 (magnesium) is 2,8,2 — filling each shell to its maximum before starting the next.

questions.stem: Two elements have electronic configurations of 2,1 and 2,8,1. Which statement about their chemical reactivity is correct?

options.text: They will have completely different chemical properties because they have different numbers of electrons
They will react similarly because both have 1 electron in their outer shell
The element with configuration 2,1 will be more reactive because it has fewer electrons
Neither element will be reactive because they have incomplete outer shells

questions.explanation: Both elements (lithium 2,1 and sodium 2,8,1) have 1 electron in their outer shell, placing them in Group 1. Chemical properties are determined by outer shell electrons, so they both form 1+ ions and react similarly — for example, both react vigorously with water to produce hydrogen gas and a hydroxide.

questions.stem: A scientist discovers a new element with 20 electrons. Based on its electronic configuration, which known element would it behave most similarly to?

options.text: Potassium (2,8,8,1)
Argon (2,8,8)
Magnesium (2,8,2)
Chlorine (2,8,7)

questions.explanation: An element with 20 electrons has the configuration 2,8,8,2. With 2 electrons in its outer shell, it is in Group 2 — the same group as magnesium (2,8,2). This element is calcium, which behaves similarly to magnesium: both form 2+ ions, react with water, and form similar compounds.

questions.stem: An element has a full outer shell of electrons with the configuration 2,8. What can you predict about this element's chemical behaviour?

options.text: It will easily lose 8 electrons to form an 8+ ion
It will be a very reactive non-metal
It will be very unreactive because its outer shell is already full
It will gain 2 more electrons to start a third shell

questions.explanation: An element with configuration 2,8 is neon, a noble gas in Group 0. Its outer shell is completely full, giving it a very stable electronic configuration. Noble gases have no tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons, making them extremely unreactive.
